article.title: 阅读四 · 为什么艺术总爱悲伤
article.background: 人文文化随笔。讨论现代艺术为何疏离“幸福”，把商业文化、宗教与死亡意识连接起来；年长人文讲述者沉稳而有余味。

sentences.en: Many things make people think artists are weird.
sentences.zh: 许多事情都会让人觉得艺术家古怪。
prosody_focus: Many things make people think artists are weird.

segments.text: Many things make people think artists are weird.

sentences.en: But the weirdest may be this: artists’ only job is to explore emotions, and yet they choose to focus on the ones that feel bad.
sentences.zh: 但最古怪的也许是这一点：艺术家的职责就是探索情感，可他们偏偏把注意力集中在那些令人难受的情绪上。
prosody_focus: But the weirdest may be this: artists’ only job is to explore emotions, and yet

segments.text: But the weirdest may be this: artists’ only job is to explore emotions, and yet they choose to focus on the ones that feel bad.

sentences.en: This wasn’t always so.
sentences.zh: 事情并非一直如此。
prosody_focus: This wasn’t always so.

segments.text: This wasn’t always so.

sentences.en: The earliest forms of art, like painting and music, are those best suited for expressing joy.
sentences.zh: 绘画和音乐等最早的艺术形式，本来最适合表达喜悦。
prosody_focus: The earliest forms of art, like painting and music, are those best suited for ex

segments.text: The earliest forms of art, like painting and music, are those best suited for expressing joy.

sentences.en: But somewhere from the 19th century onward, more artists began seeing happiness as meaningless, phony or, worst of all, boring, as we went from Wordsworth’s daffodils to Baudelaire’s flowers of evil.
sentences.zh: 但从19世纪某个时候起，越来越多艺术家把幸福视为无意义、虚假，甚至最糟糕的——乏味；艺术也从华兹华斯的水仙花一路走到了波德莱尔的《恶之花》。
prosody_focus: But somewhere from the 19th century onward, more artists began seeing happiness

segments.text: But somewhere from the 19th century onward, more artists began seeing happiness as meaningless, phony or, worst of all, boring, as we went from Wordsworth’s daffodils to Baudelaire’s flowers of evil.

sentences.en: You could argue that art became more skeptical of happiness because modern times have seen so much misery.
sentences.zh: 你可以说，现代社会充满苦难，所以艺术才越来越怀疑幸福。
prosody_focus: You could argue that art became more skeptical of happiness because modern times

segments.text: You could argue that art became more skeptical of happiness because modern times have seen so much misery.

sentences.en: But it’s not as if earlier times didn’t know perpetual war, disaster and the massacre of innocents.
sentences.zh: 可早期时代也绝非不知持续不断的战争、灾难与无辜者遭屠杀为何物。
prosody_focus: But it’s not as if earlier times didn’t know perpetual war, disaster and the mas

segments.text: But it’s not as if earlier times didn’t know perpetual war, disaster and the massacre of innocents.

sentences.en: The reason, in fact, may be just the opposite: there is too much damn happiness in the world today.
sentences.zh: 事实上，原因可能恰恰相反：今天这个世界里的“幸福”实在太多了。
prosody_focus: The reason, in fact, may be just the opposite: there is too much damn happiness

segments.text: The reason, in fact, may be just the opposite: there is too much damn happiness in the world today.

sentences.en: After all, what is the one modern form of expression almost completely dedicated to depicting happiness?
sentences.zh: 毕竟，现代哪一种表达形式几乎完全致力于描绘幸福？
prosody_focus: After all, what is the one modern form of expression almost completely dedicated

segments.text: After all, what is the one modern form of expression almost completely dedicated to depicting happiness?

sentences.en: Advertising.
sentences.zh: 广告。
prosody_focus: Advertising.

segments.text: Advertising.

sentences.en: The rise of anti-happy art almost exactly tracks the emergence of mass media, and with it, a commercial culture in which happiness is not just an ideal but an ideology.
sentences.zh: 反幸福艺术的兴起几乎与大众媒体的出现完全同步；随之而来的商业文化中，幸福不再只是理想，而成了一种意识形态。
prosody_focus: The rise of anti-happy art almost exactly tracks the emergence of mass media, an

segments.text: The rise of anti-happy art almost exactly tracks the emergence of mass media, and with it, a commercial culture in which happiness is not just an ideal but an ideology.

sentences.en: People in earlier eras were surrounded by reminders of misery.
sentences.zh: 早期时代的人们身边到处是苦难的提醒。
prosody_focus: People in earlier eras were surrounded by reminders of misery.

segments.text: People in earlier eras were surrounded by reminders of misery.

sentences.en: They worked until exhausted, lived with few protections and died young.
sentences.zh: 他们劳动到筋疲力尽，生活缺少保障，也往往早逝。
prosody_focus: They worked until exhausted, lived with few protections and died young.

segments.text: They worked until exhausted, lived with few protections and died young.

sentences.en: In the West, before mass communication and literacy, the most powerful mass medium was the church, which reminded worshippers that their souls were in danger and that they would someday be meat for worms.
sentences.zh: 在西方，在大众传播和普及识字之前，最强大的大众媒介是教会；它不断提醒信徒，他们的灵魂处在危险中，终有一天肉身会成为虫子的食物。
prosody_focus: In the West, before mass communication and literacy, the most powerful mass medi

segments.text: In the West, before mass communication and literacy, the most powerful mass medium was the church, which reminded worshippers that their souls were in danger and that they would someday be meat for worms.

sentences.en: Given all this, they did not exactly need their art to be a bummer too.
sentences.zh: 既然现实已经如此，他们实在没必要再让艺术也来添堵。
prosody_focus: Given all this, they did not exactly need their art to be a bummer too.

segments.text: Given all this, they did not exactly need their art to be a bummer too.

sentences.en: Today the messages the average Westerner is surrounded with are not religious but commercial, and forever happy.
sentences.zh: 今天，普通西方人身边充斥的不是宗教讯息，而是商业讯息，而且永远洋溢着快乐。
prosody_focus: Today the messages the average Westerner is surrounded with are not religious bu

segments.text: Today the messages the average Westerner is surrounded with are not religious but commercial, and forever happy.

sentences.en: Fast-food eaters, news anchors, text messengers, all smiling, smiling, smiling.
sentences.zh: 快餐食客、新闻主播、发短信的人，人人都在笑、笑、笑。
prosody_focus: Fast-food eaters, news anchors, text messengers, all smiling, smiling, smiling.

segments.text: Fast-food eaters, news anchors, text messengers, all smiling, smiling, smiling.

sentences.en: Our magazines feature beaming celebrities and happy families in perfect homes.
sentences.zh: 杂志里尽是笑容灿烂的名人，以及住在完美住宅里的幸福家庭。
prosody_focus: Our magazines feature beaming celebrities and happy families in perfect homes.

segments.text: Our magazines feature beaming celebrities and happy families in perfect homes.

sentences.en: And since these messages have an agenda — to lure us to open our wallets — they make the very idea of happiness seem unreliable.
sentences.zh: 而这些讯息都有自己的目的——诱使我们打开钱包——于是连“幸福”这个概念本身都显得不再可信。
prosody_focus: And since these messages have an agenda — to lure us to open our wallets — they

segments.text: And since these messages have an agenda — to lure us to open our wallets — they make the very idea of happiness seem unreliable.

sentences.en: “Celebrate!” commanded the ads for the arthritis drug Celebrex, before we found out it could increase the risk of heart attacks.
sentences.zh: 在我们发现关节炎药物西乐葆可能增加心脏病风险之前，它的广告还在命令般地喊着：“庆祝吧！”
prosody_focus: “Celebrate!” commanded the ads for the arthritis drug Celebrex, before we found

segments.text: “Celebrate!” commanded the ads for the arthritis drug Celebrex, before we found out it could increase the risk of heart attacks.

sentences.en: But what we forget — what our economy depends on us forgetting — is that happiness is more than pleasure without pain.
sentences.zh: 但我们忘记了——而我们的经济也依赖于我们忘记——幸福绝不只是没有痛苦的愉悦。
prosody_focus: But what we forget — what our economy depends on us forgetting — is that happine

segments.text: But what we forget — what our economy depends on us forgetting — is that happiness is more than pleasure without pain.

sentences.en: The things that bring the greatest joy carry the greatest potential for loss and disappointment.
sentences.zh: 带来最大喜悦的事物，也蕴含着最大失去与失望的可能。
prosody_focus: The things that bring the greatest joy carry the greatest potential for loss and

segments.text: The things that bring the greatest joy carry the greatest potential for loss and disappointment.

sentences.en: Today, surrounded by promises of easy happiness, we need art to tell us, as religion once did, Memento mori: remember that you will die, that everything ends, and that happiness comes not in denying this but in living with it.
sentences.zh: 今天，当我们被“轻易获得幸福”的承诺包围时，我们需要艺术像过去的宗教那样提醒我们：记住你终将死去，万物终有尽头；幸福并不来自否认这一事实，而来自与之共处。
prosody_focus: Today, surrounded by promises of easy happiness, we need art to tell us, as reli

segments.text: Today, surrounded by promises of easy happiness, we need art to tell us, as religion once did, Memento mori: remember that you will die, that everything ends, and that happiness comes not in denying this but in living with it.

sentences.en: It’s a message even more bitter than a clove cigarette, yet, somehow, a breath of fresh air.
sentences.zh: 这讯息甚至比丁香烟更苦涩，却又莫名像一口新鲜空气。
prosody_focus: It’s a message even more bitter than a clove cigarette, yet, somehow, a breath o

segments.text: It’s a message even more bitter than a clove cigarette, yet, somehow, a breath of fresh air.
